title: Which layers encode the refusal decision? Locating alignment depth in activations, not just tokens

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: identifying alignment-critical layers enables targeted reinforcement (deepening alignment) and explains jailbreak mechanisms (ablation attacks). Also directly informs activation-based detection design. Multiple explicit links to safety outcomes.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Linear probing of hidden states is an established methodology. Training logistic regression classifiers per layer on one model is straightforward with scikit-learn and HuggingFace. A beginner with mentor guidance can follow the established probing pipeline.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable: one model, probe per layer, accuracy plot across layers for harmful vs benign prompts. Clear metric (probe accuracy) and clear output (layer vs accuracy curve). Well-bounded experiment that fits within 30 hours.

novelty.reasoning: This idea is directly and comprehensively addressed by multiple published works. 'Safety Layers in Aligned Large Language Models: The Key to LLM Security' (ICLR 2025) localizes safety-critical layers. 'LLMs Encode Harmfulness and Refusal Separately' (Zhao et al.) shows harmfulness and refusal are orthogonal directions at specific layers. 'The Geometry of Refusal in Large Language Models: Concept Cones and Representational Independence' shows refusal signals concentrate in deeper layers and are multi-dimensional. 'Refusal Behavior in LLMs: A Nonlinear Perspective' (arXiv:2501.08145) identifies layer-specific refusal encoding. SafeSwitch (arXiv:2502.01042) steers behavior via internal activation signals at identified layers. The proposed probe-accuracy-vs-layer plot is a subset of these published findings.
